pr.title: Fix release Auth emulator validation and add manual branch validation
pr.body:
## Summary

Cut release fails when its integration command runs without the required Firebase Auth emulator. Current master includes the merged prompt-resource extraction but retains that direct call. Reuse the maintained demo-emulator wrapper while keeping every PostgreSQL and authentication test mandatory.

A manual **validation_only** option runs the same source-validation boundary on a selected branch with disposable PostgreSQL. It uses read-only checkout permissions without persisted credentials; every candidate, registry and provider/release job is excluded. Normal releases remain restricted to master. Existing PR CI is unchanged.

Closes #45.

## Test plan

- **Current base to proposed source:** after integrating master `7688118`, the [exact-head validation-only run](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37872957939/job/113634941431) passed **325 unit tests, all 25 PostgreSQL/Auth integration tests, types and builds**, including source-free prompt-bundle coverage. Emulator/database cleanup completed; all six release jobs were skipped.
- **Affected runtime and failure boundaries:** 11 targeted local tests passed for prompt payloads, resources, source-free ESM execution and validation guards. The original six missing-emulator failures, regression rejection of the old command, and real local failure/cleanup evidence remain applicable to unchanged validation code. [Actual-base impact analysis, raw results and preserved original body](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/67ca22a9dbb9b7f31bd73e5145b394529455c8cf/impact-master7688118/README.md).

[Current PR CI passed](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37872940191), including five account-browser scenarios. The prior review-bot [quota refusal](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/46#issuecomment-6072598630) is retained; it is not a completed review of this head. Independent review/QA remains required.

This non-UI change validates the real source-check boundary, **not a complete release**: candidate creation/retirement, signing, providers, publishing and deployment were not exercised. PR42's retained evidence covered normal CI and release safeguards but missed this separate command path. Earlier run37871534382 remains evidence for its original source, not the new combined build.

commit.message:
Extract exact model prompts into versioned resources (#35)

## Summary

Little Say's model instructions and starter messages are embedded in
business logic, making prompt changes difficult to find and review. This
moves the existing text into documented top-level JSON resources with
typed validation and literal substitution. Models receive the same
requests, and parents see the same presets and behavior.

Server prompts stay server-only; shared presets use the existing
Node/Expo loading paths. Account exports are preserved. Deferred ChatGPT
grants in PR20 remain outside this change.

Closes #23.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run matching synthetic requests on actual master and the extracted
resources, including Unicode, quotes, dollar signs, braces and newlines.
| Complete serialized payloads and starter/preset outputs are
byte-identical across affected operations, picture styles, speech
languages and model selections. | [Fresh Before/After
captures](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/49195f9dd70ce9a9842c460e57348c3d73935cb2/comparison.json)
|
| Load source and source-free ESM; export web, iOS and Android. | All
three exports pass. Client bundles contain shared presets and exclude
server-prompt markers. The relocated production server returns HTTP 200
with AI disabled; invalid resources/substitutions fail clearly. |
[Runtime and bundle
checks](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/49195f9dd70ce9a9842c460e57348c3d73935cb2/runtime-report.json)
|
| Create/refine starter boards and conversations with mocked providers,
including cancellation and failed saves. | All 17 Chromium scenarios
pass; prompts, drafts, consent and recovery remain intact. | [Browser
results](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/49195f9dd70ce9a9842c460e57348c3d73935cb2/oct09-browser.log)
|

This is a non-UI extraction with unchanged request behavior; exact
payload comparison is its observable Before/After contract. Fresh
captures compare actual master `18aa7c0` with final source `29e8fa8c`.
[Source, harness and artifact
identities](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/49195f9dd70ce9a9842c460e57348c3d73935cb2/manifest.json)
and [applicability/retained
originals](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/49195f9dd70ce9a9842c460e57348c3d73935cb2/applicability.json)
are preserved outside product history.

## Supporting checks and limitations

`npm run check` passed: metadata, types, 320 tests, server build and web
export. The merged runtime dependency supports passing iOS and Android
exports. [Current-revision
CI](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37870046517)
and revision-scoped independent QA are recorded separately. The bot
[declined this revision's review solely for
quota](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/35#issuecomment-6072402436);
no completed bot review is claimed.

Docker engine execution remains unperformed; its unchanged dist-copy
contract and relocated runtime were checked. Native-device testing is
deferred. No signed build, live inference, release or deployment was
performed.

---------

Co-authored-by: Codex <codex@openai.com>

@@ -0,0 +1,19 @@
+# Prompt resources
+
+Application-authored model instructions and preset messages live here as UTF-8 JSON strings. JSON preserves significant leading/trailing whitespace and newlines independently of checkout line endings. Edit the values, not the loaders; do not trim, reflow or unify wording as part of a refactor.
+
+| Resource | Caller | Substitutions |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `server/board.json` | `apps/server/src/provider.ts`: board instructions, picture addendum, translation, transcription | None; the picture addendum starts with a newline |
+| `server/pictures.json` | `apps/server/src/picture-provider.ts`: analysis, selection, generation, review, both style briefs | `visualRules` in selection/review; `look` and JSON-serialized `concept` in generation |
+| `server/speech.json` | `apps/server/src/synthesis.ts`: Realtime speech instructions | `language` |
+| `shared/onboarding.json` | `packages/core/src/onboarding.ts`: starter concept lists and template | `concepts` |
+| `shared/conversation.json` | `apps/mobile/src/ui/AiConversation.tsx`: three suggestion messages | None; these intentionally differ from onboarding |
+
+`packages/core/src/promptResources.ts` checks required text and template fields at initialization. `{{field}}` substitution runs once with a callback, so dollar signs and template-looking text in supplied values remain literal. Request data stays in its existing JSON user message; schemas, models, options, consent, cache versions and UI labels remain with their existing owners.
+
+Shared/mobile code imports only `shared/` through `promptPresets.ts`, with no filesystem access. Server resources enter only through `apps/server/src/prompts.ts`. Static JSON imports work in `tsx` and Expo/Metro; tsup embeds them in the Node ESM output already copied by Docker. No resource reads depend on the runtime working directory or source tree.
+
+The payload and preset snapshot tests preserve SHA-256 fingerprints of complete serialized requests/text captured from master before extraction, including schemas and configured/default options. They use mocked transports, never live inference. Review intentional prompt changes against these baselines rather than blindly updating them. Resource-validation tests protect literal substitutions and clear failures. Run `npm run check`, the setup/conversation browser tests, and web/iOS/Android exports when changing the loading boundary.
+
+Deferred ChatGPT grants (PR20) are absent from this base. Their distinct prompts must be integrated separately if that work resumes.

issue.title: Run release validation with the required local Firebase Auth emulator
issue.body:
## Problem

[Cut release run 37869482322, prepare step 9](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37869482322/job/113624012903#step:9:1) failed on merged master `18aa7c0`: six Firebase integration tests stopped because the local Auth emulator was not running. The release validator invokes `test:integration` directly, while normal CI uses the emulator-wrapped `test:services`. This inherited gap remains after the separate stale-candidate fix in merged PR42 and iOS dependency fix in merged PR44.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Make release-source validation provision and stop the local demo Auth emulator around its required integration suite, reusing maintained test infrastructure and retaining PostgreSQL validation.
- Keep all authentication tests mandatory and fail closed on emulator startup or test failure. Use only local synthetic/demo identities; never production Firebase, real credentials or provider setup.
- Add a regression exercising the actual release validation command boundary so passing normal CI cannot conceal different release prerequisites. Demonstrate the original failure and corrected local emulated validation.
- Preserve candidate/source/CI guards, retirement evidence and release permissions. No real release rerun, candidate mutation, publication, EAS build, store submission, deployment or secret access.

- Provide an explicit manual validation-only option for a selected branch, using the same source validator with disposable services and read-only checkout permissions. Exclude all candidate, registry, provider and publication jobs; preserve normal default-branch release guards and existing PR CI coverage.

## Implementation plan

Use a fresh isolated checkout of actual master; inspect the exact failed log and compare `scripts/release/candidate.ts`, package scripts and CI. Fix the smallest validation boundary, verify emulator lifecycle and failure propagation, and run affected maintained checks. Publish a focused draft follow-on PR with retained exact evidence and independent same-QA review. Original PR42, issue41 and their evidence remain closed/preserved.

## Implementing Codex task

Implementing task: `01a11c57-01a2-71f9-b53f-cbdee7d9b02e`. The original dirty PR42 checkout remains preserved; this correction uses a separate branch.

## Implementing PR

[Draft PR46 — release Auth emulator validation and manual branch validation](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/46). Historical related work: [PR42](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/pull/42), [issue41](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/issues/41), and [release orchestration issue27](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/issues/27).

@@ -2,6 +2,10 @@
 
 Run **Cut release** in GitHub Actions on the repository default branch (`master`). It plans changes, prepares a protected version PR, and publishes the selected GHCR image, EAS cloud builds, store submissions, and compatible OTA updates. Merges run CI only. Server deployment and device installation remain separate local operations.
 
+To validate a proposed change before merging, select its branch and enable **validation_only** in the same manual workflow. Only the read-only validation job runs: it checks out the exact run SHA without persisted credentials, runs repository checks/builds, and runs all integration tests with disposable PostgreSQL and the local `demo-little-say` Auth emulator. Emulator startup or test failure fails validation; the wrapper stops the emulator afterward. No release credentials, registry login, candidate preparation/retirement, signing, publishing or deployment runs in this mode. Normal release jobs remain restricted to the default branch through preparation. This is source validation, not proof of provider or publication behavior; `dry_run` is a separate release-planning mode with provider prerequisites.
+
+The same source-only boundary can run locally as `npm run release:validate` after `npm ci`, with an isolated PostgreSQL test database and the explicit `TEST_PG*` settings described in [testing](testing.md). It requires no release command or production Firebase project. Existing PR CI coverage is unchanged; validation-only runs are manual.
